meta.author: Śrīla Vṛndāvan Dās Ṭhākur
meta.first_line: vimala hema jini tanu anupama re!

text: vimala hema jini    tanu anupama re!
translation: His incomparable form defeats the purest gold, and is decorated with a garland of many kinds of flowers. His body is covered with goosebumps with hairs standing erect, hairs that defeat the filaments of kadamba flowers, between which are drop after drop of perspiration.

text: jini mada-matta hāti    gamana manthara ati
translation: His slow, graceful gait surpasses that of a maddened elephant. Overwhelmed with divine ecstasy, He sways and staggers as He walks. The radiance of His reddish garments eclipses the rising sun, while waves of spiritual emotion ripple across His golden form.

text: chalite nā pāre gorā-    chā̐d go̐sāñi re
bhāvete āveśa haiyā    hari hari bolāiyā
translation: Overwhelmed, Lord Gaurachandra cannot even walk. Now He cannot properly speak – only broken half-words come. Overcome with ecstatic love, He chants, “Hari! Hari!” He embraces everyone – even the lowest of persons – in His arms.

text: e sukha-sampada-kāle    gorā nā bhajinu hele
translation: Alas! At that blissful fortunate time I did not worship Lord Gaura. I did not yearn to attain His feet. In this way Vṛndāvan Dās sings the glories of Lord Chaitanyachandra and Lord Nityānanda.
